panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial cranial CT from a patient with the configured disease showing bilateral pachygyria, a recognized lissencephaly/pachygyria manifestation. B: Brain MRI from a patient with Galloway-Mowat syndrome demonstrating frontal pachygyria/gyral abnormality and deficient myelination. C: Brain MRI from a patient with Galloway-Mowat syndrome showing pachygyria with hypomyelination and white-matter T2 hyperintensity. D: Axial cranial CT from a patient with the configured disease showing bilateral cerebral pachygyria.
panels.attribution_text: Lin et al. Galloway-Mowat syndrome in Taiwan: OSGEP mutation and unique clinical phenotype.. Orphanet journal of rare diseases 2018. doi:10.1186/s13023-018-0961-9. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Brain images of the patients. a Non-contrast enhanced axial carnial CT scan of patient II at 2 days of age showed pachygyria involving bilateral cerebral hemispheres. b Axial sections of MRI of patient III-1 at 9 weeks of age showed gyral abnormalities, frontal pachygyria, and deficient myelination. c MRI of patient III-2 at 6 days of age showed pachygyria and hypomyelination with T2 high signal intensity of white matter in bilateral frontal and temporal lobes. d Non-contrast enhanced axial carnial CT scan of patient V at 1 month of age showed pachygyria involving bilateral cerebral hemispheres
in_text_mentions: Overall, 4 of our patients had been examined by cranial MRI after birth which revealed pachygyria and hypomyelination (Fig. 5) [15–17]. Patient II and patient V were examined by cranial computed tomography (CT) scan which showed pachygyria without a definite myelin defect. However, a lack of myelin is generally too subtle to identify on CT. Only 1 patient (patient III-2) had documented cerebellar atrophy. All patients died at early childhood because of severe proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia, deterioration of renal function, and multi-organ failure (range, 2 months–1 year 9 months).Fig. 5Brain

panels.figure_caption: Clinical features of patient 1. (A) Images of faces, hands, and feet showed microcephaly, wide eye spacing, giant ear (large and soft external auricle), disordered palmar pattern, and conical fingers. (B) Brain MRIs performed at the age of 8 months: Axial T1-weighted and DWI images demonstrated an enlarged ventricular system, widened bilateral lateral fissure, anterior longitudinal fissure, and frontotemporal extracerebral space, as well as a slightly wider cerebral gyrus (white arrow). (C) Renal ultrasound disclosed enhanced renal cortex.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Renal H&E section from patient V with Galloway-Mowat syndrome showing diffuse mesangial sclerosis, a characteristic renal manifestation of the disease. B: The panel is a renal H&E image from the same Galloway-Mowat syndrome patient and demonstrates glomerular pathology with prominent podocyte hyperplasia; diffuse mesangial sclerosis is established for the case in panel a and the accompanying caption. C: Real patient renal H&E histology from the Galloway-Mowat syndrome case, showing the captioned tubular abnormalities. The findings are not represented in the supplied vocabulary. D: Real patient renal H&E histology from the Galloway-Mowat syndrome case, showing the captioned tubular epithelial injury. These specific findings are not represented in the supplied vocabulary.

panels.rationale: This is a substantial single sagittal brain MRI from a disease-focused article describing a WDR73-associated nephrocerebellar syndrome on the Galloway-Mowat spectrum. The arrow identifies clear cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, a configured Galloway-Mowat manifestation. A second arrow appears to indicate a thin corpus callosum, which is not represented in the supplied vocabulary. [raw subtype: WDR73-associated nephrocerebellar syndrome on the GMS spectrum]

panels.figure_caption: Galloway-Mowat syndrome (GMS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by microcephaly, cerebellar hypoplasia, nephrosis, and profound intellectual disability. Jinks et al. extend the GMS spectrum by identifying a novel nephrocerebellar syndrome with selective striatal cholinergic interneuron loss and complete lateral geniculate nucleus delamination, caused by a frameshift mutation in WDR73.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Real patient axial T2-weighted brain MRI from a neonate with a disease-specific simplified gyral pattern in the context of a Galloway-Mowat syndrome case report. B: Real patient follow-up brain MRI documenting progression of cerebral atrophy and widened subarachnoid spaces in Galloway-Mowat syndrome. C: Real patient axial T2-weighted brain MRI showing simplified sulcation/microlissencephaly in a sibling with Galloway-Mowat syndrome. Arrows annotate the extensive scalp fluid collection.
panels.attribution_text: Hyun et al. A familial case of Galloway-Mowat syndrome due to a novel TP53RK mutation: a case report.. BMC medical genetics 2018. doi:10.1186/s12881-018-0649-y. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Patients’ brain magnetic resonance images (MRIs). Axial T2-weighted MRI (a) of Case II-1 taken at 2 weeks of age shows a simplified gyral pattern with too few and shallow sulci and normal cortical thickness. Follow-up axial T2-weighted MR image (b) acquired at 4 months of age shows a progression of diffuse brain atrophy with subarachnoid space widening. Axial T2-weighted MRI (c) of Case II-2 obtained at 3 weeks of age shows a similar pattern of simplified sulcation as the sibling. Note extensive fluid collection in the scalp (arrows)

d clasped thumb). Massive proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and generalized edema were noted immediately after birth. Renal ultrasonography revealed bilaterally small echogenic kidneys with poor cortico-medullary differentiation. A brain MRI revealed microlissencephaly, small cerebellar hemisphere size, and decreased volume of the ventral pons (Fig. 2c). At the age of 15 days, serum albumin and creatinine levels were 2.6 g/dL and 2.88 mg/dL, respectively. The parents did not want any active treatment at this time, and the patient died at the age of 21 days due to rapidly decreasing renal function.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real neonatal upper gastrointestinal radiograph from a case report of Galloway-Mowat syndrome. The caption specifically documents upward gastric dislocation into the mediastinum compatible with congenital hiatal hernia; the in-text additionally identifies gastric volvulus. B: Real neonatal lateral upper gastrointestinal radiograph from the same Galloway-Mowat syndrome case. The caption directly supports congenital hiatal hernia, while the article text also documents associated gastric volvulus.
